extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review paper examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms. It discusses limitations of current datasets and algorithms, and future directions for VQA research.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper reviews multiple VQA datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES) with different collection methods including manual annotation via crowd-sourcing (Amazon Mechanical Turk), automatic generation from captions using NLP algorithms, and synthetic image generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments, Web Scraping, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from NYU-DepthV2 Dataset, Microsoft COCO dataset, Flickr100M/YFCC100M, and synthetic cartoon images. Questions and answers collected via human annotators or generated automatically from captions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For COCO-QA: QA pairs created from COCO image captions using an NLP algorithm. For Visual Genome: Two modes - free-form questions and region-specific question prompting using bounding-box annotations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For COCO-QA: Longer sentences broken into smaller chunks for processing, though with grammatical errors. For algorithms: Image featurization using CNNs (VGGNet, ResNet, GoogLeNet), question featurization using bag-of-words, LSTM, GRU, skip-thought vectors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers generated questions with 'Stump a smart robot' instruction, separate workers generated answers. 10 answers per question collected. For Visual7W: Multiple-choice answers include correct answer, plausible answers (collected without image), popular answers, random answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is 83.3%. For 'Why' questions, over 59% have less than three annotators giving exactly same answer. Consensus metric used: Accuracy_VQA = min(n/3,1) where n is number of annotators agreeing with algorithm.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question for COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithms for COCO-QA, CNNs for image features, LSTM/GRU for question features
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential applications: Aid to blind and visually impaired individuals to get information about images, improve human-computer interaction, image retrieval. Considered a component of a Turing Test for image understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Language biases: Many questions can be answered without image (e.g., 49.6% accuracy on COCO-VQA using question alone). Yes/no bias: 38% of questions are yes/no, 59% answered 'yes'. Answer distribution bias: Top answers cover large percentage of dataset (e.g., 82.8% for COCO-VQA top-1000). Question type bias: Certain question types (e.g., 'Is', 'Are') dominate evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size insufficient for training/evaluation (curve not asymptotic). Subjective questions without single objective answer. Grammatical errors in automatically generated questions (COCO-QA). Evaluation challenges for multi-word answers. Bias impairs algorithm evaluation. Multiple-choice evaluation allows 'gaming' by using answer choices.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and validation of VQA algorithms. Usage: Research in computer vision and natural language processing. Not recommended: Real-world deployment without addressing bias limitations.
